skill.name: browser-extension-builder
skill.description: Guides the design and implementation of Chrome, Firefox, and cross-browser extensions. It covers Manifest V3 structure, content scripts, popup UI, storage, background workers, permissions, and publishing concerns.
skill.summary: Build practical browser extensions with Manifest V3 architecture, content scripts, storage, and publishing guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static command, sensitive-key, network, blocker, and innerHTML findings are false positives caused by markdown examples, placeholder names, or fixed sample markup. No prompt injection attempt or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md. One semantic medium issue remains because the Manifest V3 template uses <all_urls> for content scripts.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the <all_urls> template with a narrow placeholder host and explain how to request only the required sites.

remediation.issue: DOM injection example may encourage unsafe habits
remediation.suggestion: Show createElement, textContent, and event listeners for injected UI examples, or clearly state that innerHTML must not include untrusted data.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Content Script Scope in Template
semantic_findings.description: The Manifest V3 template uses a content script match pattern for all URLs. If copied unchanged, the extension can run code on every visited site and access sensitive page content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The <all_urls> match is present in the template, and browser extensions with this scope gain broad page access. Confidence is not higher because the skill later warns users to request minimum permissions.

content.value_statement: Browser extension projects often fail because permissions, manifests, and runtime boundaries are confusing. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through MV3 architecture, content scripts, storage, UI, and publishing choices.
actual_capabilities: Outlines a browser extension project structure with manifest, popup, content, background, options, and icons folders.
Provides a Manifest V3 template with action popup, content scripts, service worker, and options page fields.
Demonstrates content script patterns for DOM updates, runtime messaging, and injected interface controls.
Shows Chrome storage local and sync examples, including async wrapper functions.
Explains anti-patterns for excessive permissions, heavy background work, and fragile selectors.
limitations: It provides guidance and patterns, not a complete packaged extension generator.
Example permissions and host matches must be narrowed before production use.
It does not replace Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons policy review.
The skill content does not include automated tests, build tooling, or CI configuration.

use_cases.title: Prototype a New Extension
use_cases.description: Plan the folders, manifest fields, permissions, popup flow, and first content script for a focused extension idea.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Existing Add-on
use_cases.description: Map an older extension to Manifest V3 concepts such as service workers, storage, messaging, and popup actions.

use_cases.title: Review Extension Architecture
use_cases.description: Check whether permissions, content script scope, background work, and selectors are likely to pass review and remain stable.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Extension
prompt_templates.prompt: Use browser-extension-builder to plan a Chrome extension that helps users with [goal]. Include the main files, MV3 components, minimal permissions, and first build steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Popup and Content Script Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the popup, content script, and message flow for an extension that [task]. Explain what runs in each context and how data moves safely.

prompt_templates.title: Add Storage and Background Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an architecture plan for extension settings, sync storage, local storage, and background service worker events for [extension idea]. Include failure cases.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Store Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this extension concept for Chrome Web Store readiness: [concept]. Identify risky permissions, unclear user value, privacy concerns, and cross-browser issues.

output_examples.input: Plan a browser extension that lets users save notes from selected page text.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture plan with popup actions, a content script selection workflow, storage choices, minimal permissions, and release checklist items.

output_examples.input: Review an extension idea that modifies pages on every website.
output_examples.output: A permission review that recommends narrower host matches, optional access, clear user consent, and safer content script boundaries.

output_examples.input: Modernize an older Chrome extension for Manifest V3.
output_examples.output: A migration plan covering service worker behavior, message passing, storage updates, popup changes, and store submission risks.

best_practices: Start with narrow host matches and add optional permissions only when users need them.
Keep Manifest V3 service workers small and move page-specific work into content scripts.
Review copied examples for privacy, sanitization, error handling, and store policy before release.
anti_patterns: Copying all-URL content script access into production without a clear need.
Adding broad permissions before the extension has visible user value.
Treating content scripts as trusted pages instead of hostile web environments.

faq.question: Can this skill build both Chrome and Firefox extensions?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers cross-browser extension planning, but each store and browser still needs separate compatibility checks.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete extension package?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, patterns, and implementation direction that you can apply in your project.

faq.question: Does it support Manifest V3?
faq.answer: Yes. Manifest V3 structure, service workers, content scripts, popup UI, options pages, and storage are central topics.

faq.question: Can it help reduce permission risk?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights minimum permissions, optional permissions, host matching, and store review concerns.

faq.question: Is the sample manifest production ready?
faq.answer: No. The sample must be narrowed, reviewed, tested, and adapted to the exact extension purpose.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, product engineers, and technical leads who need practical browser extension architecture guidance.
